Class QuickSort

java.lang.Object
org.troy.capstone.search_engine.sorting.QuickSort
public class QuickSort extends Object
Code is sourced from a MindTap exercise from the course, but modified to fit the project. Class provides QuickSort implementation for sorting tables based on a specified comparator.

  • Method Details

    • quickSort

      public static void quickSort(List<Row> rows, RowComparator comparator)
      Sorts a list of Rows using the QuickSort algorithm based on the provided RowComparator.
      Parameters:
      rows - The list of Rows to be sorted.
      comparator - The RowComparator used to determine the order of the Rows.
      Preconditions:
      comparator is a valid RowComparator that can compare the Rows in the list.

    • quickSort

      @Deprecated @Generated public static void quickSort(List<Row> rows, RowComparator comparator, LongWrapper time)
      Deprecated.
      This is useful for analyzing the time taken, but it is not part of the main program execution.
      Sorts a list of Rows using the QuickSort algorithm based on the provided RowComparator and records the time taken for sorting. Only used in testing so it is ignored in code coverage.
      Parameters:
      rows - The list of Rows to be sorted.
      comparator - The RowComparator used to determine the order of the Rows.
      time - An optional LongWrapper to store the time taken to perform the sort. If null, time will not be recorded.
      Preconditions:
      comparator is a valid RowComparator that can compare the Rows in the list., rows is not null and the Rows contain the correct column needed to do the sorting.
      Postconditions:
      The list of Rows is sorted in place based on the order defined by the comparator, and the time taken for sorting is recorded in the provided LongWrapper if it is not null.

    • quickSort

      private static void quickSort(List<Row> rows, int low, int high, RowComparator comparator)
      Helper method for the QuickSort algorithm that recursively sorts the list of Rows based on the provided RowComparator.
      Parameters:
      rows - The list of Rows to be sorted.
      low - The starting index of the portion of the list to be sorted.
      high - The ending index of the portion of the list to be sorted.
      comparator - The RowComparator used to determine the order of the Rows.
      Preconditions:
      low and high are valid indices within the bounds of the Rows list, and low is less than high., comparator is a valid RowComparator that can compare the Rows in the list.
      Postconditions:
      The portion of the list of Rows between the low and high indices is sorted in place based on the order defined by the comparator.

    • partition

      static int partition(List<Row> rows, int low, int high, RowComparator comparator)
      Partitions the list of Rows based on the provided RowComparator and returns the index of the pivot element after partitioning.
      Parameters:
      rows - The list of Rows to be partitioned.
      low - The starting index of the portion of the list to be partitioned.
      high - The ending index of the portion of the list to be partitioned.
      comparator - The RowComparator used to determine the order of the Rows for partitioning.
      Returns:
      The index of the pivot element after partitioning.
      Preconditions:
      low and high are valid indices within the bounds of the Rows list, and low is less than high., comparator is a valid RowComparator that can compare the Rows in the list.
      Postconditions:
      The portion of the list of Rows between the low and high indices is partitioned in place based on the order defined by the comparator, and the index of the pivot element after partitioning is returned.

    • swap

      private static void swap(List<Row> rows, int i, int j)
      Swaps two elements in the list of Rows.
      Parameters:
      rows - The list of Rows in which the elements will be swapped.
      i - The index of the first element to be swapped.
      j - The index of the second element to be swapped.
      Preconditions:
      i and j are valid indices within the bounds of the Rows list.
      Postconditions:
      The elements at indices i and j in the list of Rows are swapped.
